body: dupe of #3348.   However as far as non-primary mappers I regularly debate removing this feature altogether and I've not seen someone using an NP in a standalone fashion as you're doing for many years.  Can you please describe your use case over on #3348?   that would allow the non-primary mapper feature to be better defined.
ah, this is not what I thought.

so, your non-primary mapper doesn't have "parent".   If you add that, it works:

```
mapped_child = orm.mapper(
    Child, aliased_child, non_primary=True,
    properties={
        'parent': orm.relationship(Parent)
    })

```


I don't see, at the moment, how it would be possible for the loader options to examine both the non-primary and the primary mapper at the same time.  for example if you said "joinedload('parent')", that raises an attribute error right now.  should it be looking at the primary mapper to figure these things out?   that's not possible without there being a relationship on the NP such that things like the join condition and all that can be worked out.

but there is the area of attributes that are on the object once loaded, which have loader behaviors that are essentially from the primary mapper, such as lazyload of parent.   even eager loaders that run on "secondary" could in theory work here, e.g. first query is against the NP mapper, then a "selectin" load runs against the primary mapper?   is that what someone would want?

issue.title: selectinload seems to not recognize non-primary mapper path whereas subqueryload/joinedload does

labels.name: loader options

labels.name: non-primary mappers
labels.description: things to do with the soon-to-be-deprecated non primary mapper feature

issue.body:
something is up local to the selectinload option on this one, taken from #4421

```
#!/usr/bin/env python

import sqlalchemy

from sqlalchemy import Column, ForeignKey, Integer, create_engine, orm
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base

Base = declarative_base()


class Parent(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'parents'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


class Child(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'children'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    parent_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey(Parent.id), nullable=False, index=True)
    parent = orm.relationship(Parent, backref='children')


aliased_child = sqlalchemy.select([Child]).alias()
mapped_child = orm.mapper(
    Child, aliased_child, non_primary=True,
    properties={
        'parent': orm.relationship(Parent)
    }
)

engine = create_engine('sqlite://', echo=True)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
DBSession = orm.sessionmaker(bind=engine)
session = DBSession()

parent = Parent(id=0)
child = Child(id=1, parent_id=0)
session.add_all([parent, child])
session.commit()

# works
session.expunge_all()
child = session.query(mapped_child).options(orm.subqueryload('parent')).first()
assert 'parent' in child.__dict__


# works
session.expunge_all()
child = session.query(mapped_child).options(orm.joinedload('parent')).first()
assert 'parent' in child.__dict__

# does not work
session.expunge_all()
child = session.query(mapped_child).options(orm.selectinload('parent')).first()
assert 'parent' in child.__dict__

```

body:
Example above was synthetic demo.

I use NP mapper to make row-limited relationship as described here:
https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/orm/join_conditions.html#row-limited-relationships-with-window-functions

It looks like this
```python

class Answer(Base):
   ...
   question_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey(Question.id))
   # there are some other relationships to authors, tags, comments etc.

class Question(Base):
   ...

partition = select([
    Answer,
    func.row_number().over(
        order_by=Answer.rating.desc(),
        partition_by=Answer.question_id
    ).label('index')
]).alias()

non_primary_mapper_for_answer = mapper(Answer, partition, non_primary=True)

Question.top_rated_answer = relationship(
    non_primary_mapper_for_answer,
    primaryjoin=and_(
        non_pirmary_mapper_for_answer.c.question_id == Question.id,
        non_pirmary_mapper_for_answer.c.index == 1
    )
)

```
So when i do ```session.query(Question).options(noload('*'), selectinload('top_rated_answer'))```
i get top_rated_answer, and it's relationship attributes (eg. author) lazily loads when accessed. I found no way to set load strategy for them.

issue.title: allow relationship to AliasedClass and get rid of non primary mappers
issue.body:
will replace #3348 #4422 #4421


taking the example from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/orm/join_conditions.html?highlight=partitioned#row-limited-relationships-with-window-functions , it would be mapped as:

```
class A(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'a'

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


class B(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'b'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    a_id = Column(ForeignKey("a.id"))
    cs = relationship("C")


class C(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'c'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    b_id = Column(ForeignKey('b.id'))

partition = select([
    B,
    func.row_number().over(
        order_by=B.id, partition_by=B.a_id
    ).label('index')
]).alias()

partitioned_b = aliased(B, alias=partition)

A.partitioned_bs = relationship(
    partitioned_b,
    primaryjoin=and_(partitioned_b.a_id == A.id, partition.c.index < 10)
)

```

the non primary mapper has no queryable alias making it very difficult to query from, and additionally acts in this detached way vs. it's original mapped class that nobody needs (e.g. doesn't inherit properties).  AliasedClass already does the thing that people need from np mappers, which is, load the class from a different selectable.  all that is missing is for relationship to be able to point to it.  make that happen and non primary mappers can finally be removed.

**note  - this answer is all wrong, please ignore**

OK, first off the query there should be (using the documentation mappings):

```
for a1 in s.query(A).options(noload('*'), selectinload(A.partitioned_bs).noload('*')):
    for b in a1.partitioned_bs:
        assert 'some_data' not in b.__dict__

```

and it does not work, and this is *another* bug that is not what's originally shown here nor is it being fixed by the patch in #3348.

non primary mappers are definitely going away.  I will create a system by which a normal AliasedClass can be used instead.
OK sorry, in your case "author" is a relationship, noload('*') is only for relationships, I'm working on three things at once here let me try to get only correct statements on this ticket.

I'm back to where we started on this one.  I have a nicer way of doing this I'm going to try to do for #4423, but for what you have here, using relationship to non primary, as long as I add the property to the non primary mapper, it does what you are looking for, please see the script below that illustrates.  I'm not sure that other kinds of loading like subqueryload() or selectinload() off of the "B" are possible however, I'm getting mixed results.

Please confirm that solves your immediate issue, and I'm going to look into having a more comprehensive way of allowing these non-primary mappings to work like regular aliases using AliasedClass.

```

from sqlalchemy import *
from sqlalchemy.orm import *
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declared_attr

Base = declarative_base()


class A(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'a'

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


class B(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'b'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    a_id = Column(ForeignKey("a.id"))
    c_id = Column(ForeignKey("c.id"))
    c = relationship("C")


class C(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'c'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)

partition = select([
    B,
    func.row_number().over(
        order_by=B.id, partition_by=B.a_id
    ).label('index')
]).alias()

partitioned_b = mapper(B, partition, non_primary=True, properties={
    "c": relationship(C)
})

A.partitioned_bs = relationship(
    partitioned_b,
    primaryjoin=and_(partitioned_b.c.a_id == A.id, partitioned_b.c.index < 10)
)

e = create_engine("postgresql://scott:tiger@localhost/test", echo=True)
Base.metadata.drop_all(e)
Base.metadata.create_all(e)

s = Session(e)
s.add(A(id=1))
s.flush()
s.add_all([B(a_id=1, c=C()) for i in range(100)])
s.commit()

for a1 in s.query(A).options(noload('*'), selectinload(A.partitioned_bs)):
    for b in a1.partitioned_bs:
        assert b.c is None



```

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Implement relationship to AliasedClass; deprecate non primary mappers** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1059
